main_text.p: velit offendere officium patrisfamilias, vel praecepto-ris, dicit illud contineri modis docendi & implendi, quos eo, quem indigitavimus, percurrit ordine.

Hæc de philosophiæ practicæ subiecto:objectum sequitur, videlicet res contingentes, pendentes ab hominis voluntate, ut eas possit producere, vel suspendere. Græci vocant τὰ πρακτὰ, quæ veniunt communi Juris & Justitiæ nomine.
Media hic sunt ut supra: nisi quòd tempus pomeridianum ab Aristotele deputatum sit studiis practicis.
main_text.head: Cap. L. De alphabeto philosophiæ poëticæ.
main_text.p: PHilosophiæ poëticæ alphabetum itidem habet Subjectum, Objectum & Media.Alphabetū philosophiç poëticæ.
Subjectum est Homo, quoad mentem & ingenium ποιητικὸν[?], factivum, ex peculiari temperamento dependens.
Hic sunt principia iterum interna & externa.
Interna sunt tum prima, tum orta.
Principia interna prima sunt in viribus animi superioribus & inferioribus[?].

In superioribus; puta in intellectu, ubi est vis partim generalis inveniendi & judicandi τὰ ποιη-τικά, i.e. quæ arte produci possunt; partim specialis, numerandi, mensurandi, ponderandi, fabricandi: & in voluntate, ubi est appetitus & proclivitas ad τὰ ποιητικά.

page.notes: Left edge fragments (il-, o-, e-, as, o, es, etc.) belong to the neighbouring page and were not transcribed. Greek in "Δεω-λινά" (heading note and text) is doubtful: the letters are blurred. Greek "ποιητικὸν" and "ποιη-τικά" are read from a blurred scan. The mark after "inferioribus" is a smudge or stain, possibly the start of a letter, so it is marked [?]. The decorative woodcut rule under the Greek line is not text and was left out. Catchword "ποιητικά." sits at the left, not the right; it is kept as printed.
